Title: [JOURNEY] Switching company mid-session re-homes BOTH earning and spending — the newly active company's pool moves and the other one does not
Preconditions:
[PRE:CLEAR_SESSION]
[PRE:SIGNIN_AS:MULTI_ORG_TF_BR_ALT]
[PRE:RESET_CART]
Store {{STORE_ID}} is in Organization mode — the store setting Loyalty.LoyaltyBalanceCalculationMode reads "Organization". This is NOT the ambient state of the environment (the platform default is "Customer", which the rest of the loyalty corpus assumes), so the run sets it before this suite and restores it after; a case that finds the store in Customer mode must report BLOCKED rather than assert.
WHAT THIS CASE ADDS THAT NOTHING ELSE COVERS: measured across the whole suite corpus on 2026-09-14, 72 cases earn or redeem loyalty points and 93 cases switch the active organization, and the two sets do not intersect at a single case. LOYORG-E2E-003 switches and READS; the journey cases earn and redeem inside ONE organization. So AC1 (multiple managers can purchase and earn for the same outlet) and AC2 (a manager can redeem points of the outlet) are proven only while the active company never changes — and the active company is exactly what selects the pool.
WHY THE SEAM IS WHERE THE DEFECT WOULD BE: read from source at vc-module-loyalty PR #17 head, every order-earn branch of LoyaltyProgramHandler does only this — if the store calculates balances per organization, the loyalty context OrganizationId is set to the ORDER OrganizationId — with no contact or member lookup at all. The pool an accrual lands in is therefore the ORDER organization, which the storefront cart inherits from the organization_id claim on the caller token, which is re-minted by the organization switcher. A switch that does not re-mint the claim, or a cart that keeps the pre-switch claim, credits the WRONG company with no error anywhere.
@td(MULTI_ORG_TF_BR_ALT.email) is the FRONTEND-lane multi-organization fixture — one account in TWO organizations with distinct per-organization roles. Its backend twin MULTI_ORG_TF_BR must NOT be used here: the two lanes own independent membership rows, and swapping them makes both lanes report confident wrong results.
DECIDABILITY: both companies hold DISTINCT non-zero pooled balances (@td(MULTI_ORG_LOY_POOLS.techflow_balance_at_seed) against @td(MULTI_ORG_LOY_POOLS.buildright_balance_at_seed)), and the account own user-scope balance @td(MULTI_ORG_LOY_POOLS.user_balance_at_seed) is distinct from both, so a correct scoped write, a write into the previously active company, and a fallback to the account own user scope are THREE distinguishable outcomes rather than two. Against a set of pools that all read zero this case decides nothing and must record BLOCKED, not a pass.
THE EARN QUANTITY IS NOT LOAD-BEARING and is fixed at 1: the discriminator here is WHICH pool moves, never by how much, so no quantity divergence is needed and none is claimed.
A loyalty balance CANNOT be reset on this platform — vc-module-loyalty exposes the operation log read-only, with no balance set/debit API — so every figure below is a RELATIVE DELTA against a value read immediately before the action, never an absolute number, and this case is not idempotent: it moves a real pool by a real amount every time it runs.
STATED LIMIT — the cart is EMPTY across the switch. Whether a cart BUILT under one company and CHECKED OUT after switching to another follows the cart original claim or the re-minted one is a second, narrower seam this case deliberately does not enter, because mixing the two would make an unexpected result unattributable. It is reported as a residual gap.

Cross_Layer_Checks:
[API] capture the /graphql requests for both checkouts and decode the bearer token: its organization_id claim must name ORG_2 on both. A token still carrying ORG_1 is the direct form of the defect, and it localises the fault to the switcher rather than to the loyalty handler
[API] read the organization-scoped operation log for both companies (GET {{BACK_URL}}/api/loyalty-program-operation-log/balance/organization/{id}) and confirm the Earned and Redeemed rows for ORDER_EARN and ORDER_SPEND carry the ORG_2 OrganizationId — the ledger is the durable form of the claim, independent of what the account page renders
[API] read the account OWN user-scope balance (GET {{BACK_URL}}/api/loyalty-program-operation-log/balance/user/{userId}) before and after: it must be unchanged. A user-scope movement means the handler fell back to user scope instead of resolving an organization, which is the third distinguishable outcome and is neither a pass nor the stale-claim defect
[API] if BAL_ORG1_BEFORE equals BAL_ORG2_BEFORE, the pools are not distinguishable on this environment — record BLOCKED and re-seed rather than recording a pass
[API] a co-settling mission grant would also move a pool — check the organization ledger for a mission-sourced row before attributing any delta to this order
[CONSOLE] no unhandled JS error during either switch or either checkout
[NETWORK] no 4xx/5xx on /graphql during any page load in the journey
Failure_Signals:
BAL_ORG1_AFTER is greater than BAL_ORG1_BEFORE while company 2 was the active company throughout — the accrual landed in the previously active company pool (stale organization_id claim)
MID-JOURNEY — the cart badge drops to 0 immediately after the company switch, or the cart page shows a different set of lines than before the switch
MID-JOURNEY — the account context header shows ORG_2 but the points-history figure is still BAL_ORG1_BEFORE until a hard reload (stale Apollo cache, so the page and the token disagree about which company is active)
the points-priced line is refused at the cart with an insufficient-balance message although BAL_ORG2_BEFORE was positive — the validator resolved a different scope than the page rendered (BL-LOY-008)
neither pool moves while the account own user-scope balance does — the handler fell back to user scope
no balance settles within the 40s budget (report BLOCKED, do not force an assertion)
both pools read zero at baseline (inconclusive, never a pass)
Cleanup: Restore ORG_1 as the active company and sign out — the active company is per-account state a later case would otherwise inherit. Remove any leftover cart lines first. The two orders and the points they moved are NOT reversible (BL-LOY-019), so the pools end at new values by design and every later assertion must read them fresh rather than reuse a figure from this run.
